note: Both texts are complete; X keeps the Greek 'ἐκ γενέσεως' and 'sit', while Y gives 'ex γενέσεως', 'fit' and joins 'extincturis', which are minor slips.
Y modernises spellings ('affirmirt', 'präsentire euch' for 'affirmiert', 'præsentiere eüch') and misreads 'heüttgen' for 'heütigen'; the wording is otherwise the same.
The leaf reads 'Acorum ... iridis radicibus' and 'Allec pisciculus dicitur'; X garbles these as 'Aesum ... indeta dicitur' and 'Alleluia siculi dicitur', and many other entries are wrong as well.
Y normalises printed spellings ('vierten', 'Geiz', 'sollst', 'stürzete' for 'vierdten', 'Geitz', 'solst', 'stürtzete'); the content is otherwise identical.

X gives a readable expansion that follows the manuscript, whereas Y is largely meaningless pseudo-abbreviation (e.g. 'Cereb̃ septẽ nuoz̃ p̃aia' for 'A cerebro septem nervorum paria') and invents a page number '22'.
X puts the left half-leaf before the right (the text starts at '髻齔時') and misreads '閣皁' as '閱皁', '二名' as '亦名' and '處' as '慶'; Y has the right order and readings.
Y normalises 'Sol dis' to 'Soll dis' and 'wuste' to 'wußte'; the text is otherwise the same.
The leaf reads 'Hexen-Proceß' and 'Hexerey', and the name is 'Malbosson'; Y repeatedly misreads these as 'Heren-Proceß', 'Hererey' and 'Malboffon'.
Y misreads 'hiebey' as 'hieben'; otherwise the two are identical apart from bold markup.
The final 'Ad' on the leaf is the first word of the next sentence, not a catchword; X keeps it in the text, while Y moves it to a catchword. The two differ otherwise only in italics.
